decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-2097979473 (fragments f01 and f02) directly supports the claim. The source describes a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EML4-ALK fusion who was treated with crizotinib. The patient achieved an initial partial response but progressed after 5 months. Molecular analysis at relapse identified the ALK C1156Y variant, which was not present before treatment. In vitro assays using Ba/F3 cells expressing the EML4-ALK C1156Y fusion showed reduced sensitivity to crizotinib compared to wildtype, and immunoblotting confirmed that crizotinib failed to inhibit tyrosine phosphorylation of the mutant fusion. These findings confirm that the emergence of the ALK C1156Y variant at relapse following crizotinib treatment is associated with clinical resistance and reduced drug sensitivity.

citations.quote: A 28 year-old patient with T4N3M1 stage lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EML4-ALK variant 1 fusion was treated with crizotinib after failing conventional therapy. The patient achieved a partial response, but progressed after 5 months of treatment. Molecular analysis at relapse identified C1156Y in the ALK kinase domain of the fusion at an allele frequency of 41.8%. This variant was undetected by Sanger sequencing in the tumor collected before crizotinib treatment. Cytotoxicity assays revealed Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK C1156Y were more resistant to crizontinib than those expressing
EML4-ALK wildtype. Immunoblot demonstrated crizontinib reduced tyrosine phosphorylation of the wildtype fusion, but not the EML4-ALK C1156Y fusion.

findings.statement: In a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EML4-ALK fusion, the emergence of the ALK C1156Y variant at relapse following crizotinib treatment is associated with clinical resistance, as evidenced by progression after an initial partial response and confirmed by in vitro assays showing reduced crizotinib sensitivity and lack of phosphorylation inhibition in cells expressing the mutant fusion.
